security_spec.violation_condition: M-mode RNMI handler code (in OpenSBI firmware or bhyve host context) reads or writes mnstatus.MNPV on a hart that implements Smrnmi but not the H extension, treating a reserved-zero bit as valid virtualization state, causing incorrect context save/restore decisions when an RNMI fires during FreeBSD kernel execution in S-mode or VS-mode.
security_spec.summary: M-mode RNMI handler incorrectly relying on mnstatus.MNPV without gating on H extension presence can corrupt virtualized-context restoration on bare-metal FreeBSD systems

findings.finding: FreeBSD's RISC-V trap handler (exception.S) does not implement any Smrnmi/RNMI/mnstatus handling code. No mnstatus CSR reads, writes, or MNPV bit checks exist anywhere in the FreeBSD kernel. FreeBSD runs in S-mode (supervisor mode) and relies on OpenSBI firmware for M-mode services; RNMI handling is entirely the responsibility of M-mode firmware, not the FreeBSD kernel.
findings.snippet:
// No mnstatus, mnepc, mncause, mnscratch references found in exception.S
// No Smrnmi/RNMI CSR handling anywhere in sys/riscv/

findings.finding: The bhyve VMM instruction emulator does not implement CSR emulation for mnstatus (0x744), mnepc (0x741), mncause (0x742), or mnscratch (0x740). No Smrnmi CSR virtualization exists in the FreeBSD hypervisor, so there is no code that could incorrectly read or write mnstatus.MNPV for a guest.
findings.snippet: // No CSR_* or csr references to 0x740-0x744 or mnstatus in vmm_instruction_emul.c

findings.finding: VM_INTINFO_NMI (2 << 8) is a generic VMM interrupt information type constant for virtual NMI injection, not related to Smrnmi/mnstatus CSR access. This is standard VMM interrupt classification and does not involve reading or writing mnstatus.MNPV. It is unrelated to the security spec concern.
